board.note: Rebuilt after a fair complaint: the first version of this board was nine lines and every one of them was written between 1961 and 1986, which is a record of where I went looking rather than of anything about you. The five most concentrated of those are retired here. What is left spans 1792 to 2024 — Wollstonecraft on why power would rationally keep people ignorant, Hirschman and Simon on how projects and systems actually survive, Sutton on thirty years of researchers losing to their own cleverness, and three lectures from the last five years by a Filipino journalist, a Norwegian playwright and a Korean novelist. Four of the nine are from this century and three from the last five years, against a collection that runs 28 per cent and 18 per cent. Also worth saying plainly: seventeen of the eighteen authors you currently hold are men, so a third of this board is not.
